event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: American Tower’s February 25 2021 filing discusses COVID-19 as a still-unfolding, high-severity external shock.  Because the pandemic began less than a year before the report, the Time Decay Principle allows high scores.  The disclosures consistently frame the virus as a live, multi-dimensional threat rather than a historical footnote: (i) weakened tenant finances and consumer demand could cut lease revenue; (ii) supply-chain blockages, social-distancing measures and workforce shortages could slow site builds, integrations and maintenance; (iii) capital-market volatility and currency swings could hamper both AMT’s and its tenants’ financing; and (iv) government lockdowns and travel bans could directly curtail operations.  Although the language is largely forward-looking and qualitative (no quantified dollar impacts), it repeatedly uses strong materiality wording (“materially and adversely affect,” “material adverse effect”) and specifies concrete channels—equipment procurement, liquidity, FX volatility, credit ratings, site access.  There are few mitigating statements and no firm offsets.  Accordingly, COVID-19 constitutes a significant, continuing risk whose evidentiary sentences merit upper-mid scores (6-8) within the 0-10 scale for a very recent event.

evidence_list.snippet: The financial condition of wireless service providers, including as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic;

components.reason: Identifies pandemic-driven deterioration in tenants’ financial condition as a risk driver that could lower leasing demand.
Generic and forward-looking with no quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Links tenants’ health to COVID-19 but in a brief, unquantified manner—moderate recent-event risk.

evidence_list.snippet: a decrease in consumer demand for wireless services, including due to general economic conditions, disruption in the financial and credit markets or global social, political or health crises, such as the material adverse effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on the global economy and markets;

components.reason: Connects pandemic to a ‘material adverse effect’ on global economy and wireless demand.
Specifies concrete impact channel (consumer demand).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Explicitly cites COVID-19 as materially harming demand, but still qualitative.

evidence_list.snippet: The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic could materially and adversely affect our tenants through disruptions of, among other things, their ability to procure telecommunications equipment through their supply chains and their ability to maintain liquidity and deploy network capital, with potential decreases in consumer spending contributing to liquidity risks.

components.reason: Direct linkage of pandemic to ‘materially and adversely’ affecting tenants.
Details concrete mechanisms: supply-chain disruption and liquidity constraints.
Uses strong ‘could materially and adversely affect’ language.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Rich, specific description of severe, current tenant-level impacts—high severity score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, many of our tenants and potential tenants rely on capital raising activities to fund their operations and capital expenditures, which may be more difficult or expensive in the event of downturns in the economy or disruptions in the financial and credit markets, such as the current environment driven by the significant disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Highlights pandemic-driven market disruptions impeding tenant financing.
Connects financing stress to reduced cap-ex, indirectly threatening AMT revenue.
Forward-looking without quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows specific financial-market channel and materiality, so strong but not maximal.

evidence_list.snippet: Additionally, temporary business closures, social distancing measures and the potential unavailability of key personnel or a significant number of our employees as a result of COVID-19 are difficult to predict, and may have a negative impact on the timely and efficient integration of operations, telecommunications infrastructure assets and personnel.

components.reason: Lists concrete operational impediments (closures, distancing, staffing).
Links directly to integration delays of assets—strategic impact.
Acknowledges unpredictability, adding uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Operational integration risk from pandemic restrictions—high but not quantified.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, extreme market volatility and disruption caused by COVID-19 may impact our ability to raise additional capital through debt and equity financing activities or our ability to repay or refinance maturing liabilities, or impact the terms of any new obligations, which in turn may have an adverse impact on our credit ratings.

components.reason: Identifies pandemic’s effect on AMT’s own financing and capital-market access.
Specifies potential downgrade of credit ratings—serious financial consequence.
Scenario-based and qualitative.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct corporate-level financing and credit-rating risk from COVID-19—strong evidence.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, federal, state and local governments in many of our markets have recently taken actions to contain the spread of COVID-19, including travel bans, quarantines, shelter-in-place orders and business shutdowns, among others, and may take additional actions in the future.

components.reason: Enumerates specific restrictive government measures linked to COVID-19.
Notes possibility of further actions, extending risk horizon.
No quantified impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Details concrete regulatory constraints; risk clear but not yet tied to dollar impact.

evidence_list.snippet: These governmental actions could remain effective for a prolonged period of time with potential material adverse impacts on our, and our tenants’, business operations.

components.reason: Warns of prolonged restrictions causing ‘material adverse’ operational impacts.
Covers both company and tenant effects.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong wording on duration and severity, though still qualitative.

evidence_list.snippet: Volatility in foreign currency exchange rates, which has recently increased as a result of uncertainties caused by COVID-19, can also affect our ability to plan, forecast and budget for our international operations and expansion efforts.

components.reason: Links pandemic-driven FX volatility to planning/budgeting difficulties.
Applies across international operations, broadening scope of risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows financial-planning risk from pandemic-induced currency swings—moderately severe.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, any damage or destruction to, or inability to access, our towers, fiber networks, data centers or computer systems, as a result of measures implemented in response to COVID-19 or otherwise, may cause supply chain delays or impact our ability to provide services to our tenants and lead to tenant loss, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations or financial condition.

components.reason: Describes direct operational disruption and infrastructure inaccessibility due to COVID-19 measures.
Links to supply-chain delays, service interruption and tenant loss with ‘material adverse effect’.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete scenario impacting core assets and revenues with strong materiality language—high severity.

evidence_list.snippet: As further set forth in Item 1A of this Annual Report under the captions “Risk Factors,” the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, as well as the response to mitigate its spread and effects, may adversely impact us and our tenants and the demand for our communications sites in the United States and globally.

components.reason: Summarizes broad adverse impacts on company, tenants and demand worldwide.
Applies globally, indicating wide geographic reach of risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Captures enterprise-wide demand and operational risk, but without specific mechanisms or figures.
